title: Chapter 28: Different From What You Told Us
html:
“They’re coming today?” Chen Ge was not particularly worried.

“I’m betraying my own side by warning you. They want to film a funny video inside your Haunted House and post it online to cheer Senior Gao up. Please don’t take it personally. Our program has only a handful of girls, and you managed to scare the most popular one. Anyway, I hear footsteps—I have to go.” He San hung up at once.

They want to film a comedy video in my Haunted House?Chen Ge put away his phone, and a mischievous smile slowly appeared.Medical students are supposed to have strong nerves. They’ll make ideal test visitors for the new scenario. Let’s see who is laughing when they come out.

After lunch, Chen Ge reopened the entrance. Visitors who had missed the morning session quickly filled the queue. Some had come because of his videos and livestream, others had been dragged along by friends or family, and a few joined simply because a long line suggested the attraction must be worth trying.

“Tickets are twenty yuan. Smaller groups usually get the best experience.” Chen Ge kept the line moving while coordinating with Xu Wan. By 3:00 p.m., seven fashionably dressed university students entered New Century Park and headed straight for the Haunted House.

Their personalities seemed very different, but none of them spoke much while waiting. The group’s unusual seriousness stood out. When the previous visitors emerged leaning on one another, the tallest student stepped toward Chen Ge.

“Boss, six tickets.” His voice was low and steady.

Chen Ge counted the group behind him. “There are seven of you.”

“He’s just the guide who brought us here.” The tall student pulled He San to the front.

“Boss, I’m not going in.” He San still had vivid memories of his previous visit. He gave Chen Ge an awkward smile and immediately tried to disappear back into the group.

“You came all this way. I can’t leave you standing outside by yourself.” Chen Ge handed the tall student seven tickets. “This one’s on the house. You’re all from Jiujiang Medical University, right? Nice to meet you.”

His unexpected friendliness left several of the medical students feeling slightly embarrassed about their revenge plan.

“He San, the boss gave you a free ticket. Refusing now would be rude.” The tall student distributed the tickets. Instead of entering immediately, however, the group gathered just outside for what looked suspiciously like a tactical briefing.

“He San and I will form one team. Monkey and Lao Zhao, you’re together. Lao Song, Xiao Hui, and Shi Ling, you’re the third group. Everyone remembers the strategy we read on the forum, right?”

“Memorized.”

“He San already sketched the old layout for us, and we know the tricks he encountered last time. Stay calm, don’t panic, and whatever happens, do not embarrass Jiujiang Medical University.”

“Understood!”

“Good. From this moment on, get yourselves into the right mindset. Stay alert, keep your heads clear, and don’t let the atmosphere control you.”

“Exactly. We’re medical students. We can handle a few ghosts and props.”

“Do you remember the oath we made when we entered the university?”

“An upright heart walks an upright path! Jiujiang Medical University—speakers for the living and the dead!”

“Then let’s go!”

The speech was stirring enough that nearby visitors actually applauded. Even Chen Ge was impressed.

He San and the tall student stepped away from the group. “We’ll go first. Wait for our good news.”

The two approached Chen Ge with the solemn determination of soldiers marching into battle.

“Only the two of you?”

“Your rules say no more than three people per group, don’t they?”

“That limit is for Minghun. The new scenario can take all seven of you at once, so there’s no reason to make half the group wait.” Chen Ge led them inside. “First, everyone needs to sign the standard participation waiver and read the safety notice.”

“This wasn’t here last time.” He San drifted toward the table.

“That’s because you were my first visitor to faint inside the attraction.” Chen Ge smiled pleasantly at the students. “I’m sure He San has told you plenty about this place already, so I’ll spare you the history lesson. I only have one warning.”

His smile faded. He pulled up the morning news on his phone. “The old Ping An Apartments case had a major breakthrough last night, but one suspect still hasn’t been found. Completely unrelated, of course, but when I arrived this morning the Haunted House door was open even though I was certain I’d locked it. Both places are on the west side of town. I’m probably overthinking it.”

With a few carefully chosen sentences, Chen Ge planted exactly the doubt he wanted. He did not need them to believe the story outright; imagination could do the rest.

Once everyone had signed in, he led the group to the third floor and slowly opened the entrance to Murder by Midnight.

A cold draft slipped through the corridor. Half-open doors seemed to watch them from both sides, while stairways and narrow turns made the set feel far larger than it was. Soot-darkened ceilings, damaged walls, and old-looking scratches gave the whole place the appearance of a building abandoned after some long-ago disaster.

Much of the group’s confidence vanished the moment they saw the set. Everyone stopped and turned toward He San.

“Where’s the Siheyuan?”

“This is nothing like what you described.”

“I trained with weights all night so I’d be ready for that coffin.”

The combined stare nearly made He San wilt. He looked desperately to Chen Ge for help, but the proprietor ignored him. “This scenario is called Murder by Midnight. Please don’t take photographs. Your goal is to find the hidden exit within twenty minutes. If anyone wants to stop early, call out toward one of the cameras and we’ll bring you out.”

Once all seven students had entered, Chen Ge gave them a final smile. “Enjoy.”
